messages:
anna: quick sync — we have two customer-driven asks to onboard models into the catalog: (A) mistral-instruct-7B (quantized runtime) and (B) llama-3-13B (fp16/quant variants). Customer CS reports: one growth SaaS wants cheaper low-latency for bursty endpoints, and an enterprise legal customer wants higher-quality 13B for complex summarization. need RICE + sequencing recommendation. constraints: Dedicated pools, private deployment packaging, and rollout gating (latency SLO, per-token cost target, eval pass rate). thoughts?

vikram: +1 on doing RICE. my gut: 7B wins reach & effort (smaller, easier quant), 13B wins impact for high-value customers.

sara: quick eval snapshot from lab: mistral-7B -> avg F1 on our summarization set 0.64, latency 45ms/token on A100-80g quant path; llama-13B -> F1 0.78, latency 120ms/token fp16. hallucination rate (measured) 7B 8%, 13B 4%.

leo: from CS — the enterprise legal team is explicit: quality matters more than cost for their workflows, but they'd be OK joining a closed beta. Growth SaaS mostly cares about cost and latency.

mike_p: tradeoff framing: sequence by expected revenue lift / support cost. If we ship 7B first we capture broad PLG momentum, but we risk CS churn if enterprise feels deprioritized. proposal: ship 7B to hosted + dedicated (low-friction), run a 13B closed beta for enterprise with SLA/observability hooks.

eva: to make that concrete i put together a short RICE calc. please react with :+1: if you agree or :thinking_face: for concerns.

```
Candidate A: mistral-instruct-7B (quant)
Reach = 60 (PLG + growth SaaS)   Impact = 5 (moderate quality uplift)   Confidence = 0.7   Effort = 3 -> RICE = (60*5*0.7)/3 = 70

Candidate B: llama-3-13B
Reach = 20 (enterprise closed beta) Impact = 9 (high quality)    Confidence = 0.6   Effort = 8 -> RICE = (20*9*0.6)/8 = 13.5

Notes: numbers normalized to our feature scoring scale. A higher RICE suggests 7B should be prioritized for broad availability, while 13B is high-impact but high-effort.
```

eva: gating checklist (proposed) for catalog entry and GA:
- perf baseline (latency under SLO per deployment class)
- cost estimate & per-token simulation in Console
- eval pass (automated eval harness) >= target quality threshold
- rollout plan w/ canary and automatic fallback
- docs + sample prompts + token accounting examples

vikram: implementation notes: 7B quant path needs kernel selection + KV cache tuning; effort=3 assumes reuse of existing quant pipeline. 13B effort=8 includes optimized kernels + memory/pin optimizations for Dedicated plus packaging for Private.

sara: small ask: define "eval pass" thresholds. propose: summarization F1 >= 0.60, hallucination <= 6% for GA. 7B may pass F1 but not hallucination target — we can accept a higher hallucination for GA if we add explicit warnings and safety mitigations.

leo: enterprise customer will accept closed beta if we provide logs & higher observability and an SLA test window. they want the ability to pin model version.

mike_p: scope negotiation: reduce GA scope for 13B to "private + dedicated closed beta" only, not hosted GA. that cuts effort/QA surface.

deploy-bot: scheduled-ci:catalog-integration #1829876 started — integration tests queued for mistral-instruct-7B quant path. ETA 2h.

anna: summary & decision:
- APPROVE sequence: onboard mistral-instruct-7B to hosted + dedicated GA first.
- RUN llama-3-13B as a closed beta (private + dedicated) with enterprise customers and a separate rollout ticket.
- ACTIONS: @vikram to own 7B integration (ETA 2 weeks), @sara to finalize eval thresholds and run full eval suite, @eva to draft rollout checklist & pricing impact notes, @leo to coordinate closed-beta customers.

please react if any objections. going to spin up the deck/PR for roadmap board after consensus. :rocket!
